title: Complete Shutter Down Paralyzes Rawalakot Poonch as Thousands Protest Against Punitive Measures, Power Cuts and Communication Blackouts
excerpt: Thousands shut down Rawalakot in protest against prolonged electricity outages, low voltage supply and communication blackouts across District Poonch.
author: Special Correspondent

heroImage.caption: Residents protest prolonged power cuts and communication blackouts in Rawalakot.

items: Thousands joined a complete shutdown across Rawalakot in protest against prolonged electricity cuts
Residents report between 15 and 20 hours of daily load shedding in District Poonch
Internet and mobile services remain unreliable despite paid 4G subscriptions
Businesses, hospitals, schools and universities face severe disruption
Protesters demand restoration of electricity and communication services

body.text: A complete shutter down brought life to a standstill in Rawalakot on Monday as thousands of residents from across District Poonch poured into the streets to protest prolonged power outages, severe load shedding, low voltage electricity and persistent internet and mobile network disruptions.

Markets remained closed and traffic was largely halted as protesters marched through the city and gathered near the grid station. Demonstrators demanded an immediate end to what they described as collective punishment of the population.
Electricity cuts and communication blackouts have pushed daily life in Poonch to the brink, residents say.

body.caption: Protesters gather near the grid station demanding restoration of electricity.

body.text: Power shortages fuel growing anger

Residents say Azad Kashmir has been subjected to extreme load shedding for several months, with the Poonch region facing between fifteen and twenty hours of power cuts daily. Electricity supply remains unstable and voltage levels frequently drop below usable levels.
Internet and mobile services have also become unreliable. Even users paying for high speed mobile connections report extremely slow data speeds, interrupted calls and repeated network failures.

body.caption: Shuttered markets during the complete shutdown in Rawalakot.

body.text: The consequences have been severe across the region. Small businesses that depend on electricity and digital connectivity are struggling to survive. Hospitals and clinics report disruptions in essential services, while schools and universities say teaching and research activities are being seriously affected.

Printing presses, legal offices and online services have also suffered. Students preparing for examinations and researchers working on digital platforms report increasing difficulty accessing basic communication tools.
Diaspora families also affected

Millions of Kashmiris living abroad say they are also feeling the impact. Families report spending hours trying to contact relatives in Azad Kashmir as power cuts and network disruptions repeatedly interrupt communications.
The situation has created deep anxiety among families who depend on regular contact with loved ones in the region.
Families abroad say they often spend hours trying to reach relatives due to power cuts and failing mobile networks.
Protests follow years of frustration

Public frustration has been building for more than two and a half years. Residents across Azad Kashmir have repeatedly staged peaceful demonstrations demanding reliable electricity and access to essential services.

Earlier protests forced authorities to enter into agreements promising electricity at production cost and improvements in infrastructure. Residents now say those commitments have not been fulfilled and the situation has deteriorated further.

Protesters accuse authorities of responding to democratic demands with force, intimidation and disinformation. Several peaceful demonstrations in recent years were met with violent crackdowns that resulted in civilian deaths.
Incidents reported in Muzaffarabad in May 2024 and additional fatalities in October 2025 have further intensified public anger across the region.
Electricity surplus but continued shortages
Azad Kashmir produces more than four thousand megawatts of electricity while its daily requirement is estimated between three hundred and fifty and four hundred megawatts.

Despite this apparent surplus, residents continue to experience long power outages and unstable electricity supply. Protesters argue that the crisis is the result of political and administrative decisions rather than technical limitations.

Rights activists also point to findings in international reports, including those published by the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights in 2018 and 2019 and the European Parliament report on Kashmir in 2007.
These reports highlight serious concerns regarding human rights conditions in the region and stress the obligation to ensure access to essential services and fundamental freedoms.
Indefinite sit in announced
Protest leaders announced an indefinite sit in in Rawalakot and warned that demonstrations will continue until authorities honour all agreements previously made with the public.
Participants called for an immediate end to what they describe as collective punishment of the population, the restoration of reliable electricity supply and full access to communication networks.
Residents say the protests will continue peacefully but firmly until the basic rights and dignity of the people of Azad Kashmir are respected.
